root_cause.text: The svcrdma inline-copy path in `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()` failed to bounds-check `head->rc_curpage` before using it to index `rqstp->rq_pages`, allowing the Read-chunk page index to run past the allocated `rq_pages` array in the RPC request structure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message both state that `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range` “indexed rqstp->rq_pages[rc_curpage] without verifying rc_curpage stays within the allocated page array,” and the patch adds `if (head->rc_curpage >= rqstp->rq_maxpages) return -EINVAL;` before page access in `net/sunrpc/xprtrdma/svc_rdma_rw.c`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description and commit message both state that `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range` “indexed rqstp->rq_pages[rc_curpage] without verifying rc_curpage stays within the allocated page array,” and the patch adds `if (head->rc_curpage >= rqstp->rq_maxpages) return -EINVAL;` before page access in `net/sunrpc/xprtrdma/svc_rdma_rw.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to prevent `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()` from accessing pages past `rq_maxpages`.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added inside the page-processing loop in `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()`: before using `head->rc_curpage`, the code now returns `-EINVAL` if `head->rc_curpage >= rqstp->rq_maxpages`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now aborts with an invalid-argument error instead of continuing when it would advance beyond the maximum allowed request pages, preventing out-of-bounds page access or page list overrun.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check to prevent `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()` from accessing pages past `rq_maxpages`.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a bounds check in svc_rdma_copy_inline_range() to prevent head->rc_curpage from indexing past the allocated rq_pages/rq_maxpages limit.

candidates.rationale: This loop advances through pages in the inline-copy path without any bounds check on the current page index, which is the condition that allowed `head->rc_curpage` to run past `rqstp->rq_pages`.
This is part of the copy loop that consumes pages, but in the pre-fix code there was no preceding check ensuring the page index stayed within the allocated request pages.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop iterates through pages in the inline-copy path without any bounds check on the current page index, allowing `head->rc_curpage` to advance past `rqstp->rq_pages`.
This copy step consumes pages as the loop advances, and in the pre-fix code it occurred without a prior check that the page index stayed within the allocated request pages.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the shown function body is enough to determine the issue. In `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()`, the code indexes the request page array with `info->ri_pageno` without any bounds check: `head->rc_arg.pages[info->ri_pageno] = rqstp->rq_pages[info->ri_pageno];`. This is exactly the vulnerable construct described: `head->rc_curpage`/page index can run past the allocated `rq_pages` array. The function only computes `numpages` and iterates, but there is no check that `info->ri_pageno` stays within the valid number of request pages before using it. The fix is not present here because there is no guard like a limit check or early return when the page index would exceed the array; the code proceeds directly to the out-of-bounds indexing.
